text: You're in ordinary traffic, moving with everyone else. And you want one simple thing: to get ahead. A small, reasonable urge.
So you take the lane that's rolling. Seconds later, the lane you left surges past you. You feel it, and it always happens.
So you go looking for the trick. Is something watching you, picking whichever lane you leave? It isn't. Traffic moves in waves.
Then it clicks. When your lane crawls, cars pour past for minutes. When it flies, you overtake in seconds. You spend more time being passed.
And that's the price. Every losing moment gets stored. Your memory of the drive fills with the other lane winning, and it's hard to shake.
Tomorrow you're in the same traffic, and both lanes still arrive together. But now you see the wave, and it stops fooling you.
